scope: Once-only exec-pipe completion shared by the original monitor and main-thread checkin; pthread checkin performs no process replacement or fork notification.

regression.scope: Actual Call checkout/checkin, Process notifyCheckin and exec lifecycle, Thread pushCallReply and registry; real Linux pipe success EOF/failure marker, actual stored monitor callbacks dispatched in controlled order. Controlled XNU construction/destruction and output transport; no full server event loop, actual Linux exec, native Darling session, or Mach-O integration.
regression.negative_control: Exact archived stage107 Thread/Process/Call sources with matching private headers; current read-only copied non-replaced objects. Not a historical complete-server binary.

native_stage107_observation.parent_state: Original mapped mldr __darling_thread_create yields waiting for args.pth to clear.
native_stage107_observation.child_state: darling_thread_entry waits in explicit_checkin recvmsg on RPC FD 10239.
native_stage107_observation.server_observation: Server remained alive; the two corresponding child threads had no registry entries; selected inbox/outbox and client socket queues were empty.
native_stage107_observation.causal_claim: The source defect reproduces the same child self-unregistration and missing checkin reply under controlled order. The exact ordering in this native run was not recorded.

later_cancellation.reason: Confirmed thread-registration stall after 794 actions; preserve completed compiler products.
later_cancellation.Info_Template_and_rsync_diagnostics: Consequences of the unfinished/cancelled build, not proof of an independent template or rsync root cause.
later_cancellation.observer_failure: Host observer chmod failed on a root-owned nonfatal GDB core; native build continued until separately cancelled.

native_stage108_terminal_result.diagnosis: Original ld could not open the UBA temporary response file; the diagnostic named both /var/root and canonical /private/var/root aliases.
native_stage108_terminal_result.causal_limit: The new attempt passed the two previous stalled compile actions. This does not trace the earlier native exec/checkin event order or prove that the lifecycle change was its sole cause.
